lines.text: Her beloved knocks at night, his head drenched with dew, and she says she has taken off her robe.
She rises to open the door, but her beloved has turned and gone, and he does not answer her call.
The watchmen beat her and take her sandals, and she asks the daughters of Jerusalem to tell him she is sick with love.
She describes him as outstanding among ten thousand, with a head of purest gold and legs like pillars of marble set on bases of silver.
She says he has gone down to his garden to gather lilies, and that she belongs to him and he to her.
